scenes.text: Claude added one line to a migration, and the orders page went from almost two seconds to four milliseconds. Here's why.
Without an index, Postgres reads every single row, checking each one until it finds user forty-two.
An index keeps user IDs sorted in a tree. Postgres starts at the root, and only walks down the branch that can contain forty-two.
Three steps instead of a full scan. At a million orders, that's about twenty steps, instead of a million.
